records.title: Blood clot in a vein
records.summary: Swelling, pain or a cord-like vein in the neck or leg.

data.trigger: Swelling, pain or a cord-like vein in the neck or leg.
steps: Start anticoagulant only with flight surgeon agreement
Plan landing and bleeding risk with the ground team
data.comms_note: A jugular vein clot was found in an ISS astronaut during a research scan and was treated in flight.

records.title: Severe low blood sugar (unable to swallow)
records.summary: Confused or unresponsive with low blood sugar.

data.trigger: Confused or unresponsive with low blood sugar.
steps: Do not give anything by mouth

records.title: Swallowed a toxic substance
records.summary: Accidental swallowing of a chemical or medication overdose.

data.trigger: Accidental swallowing of a chemical or medication overdose.
steps: Do not make the person vomit

records.title: Acute anxiety or panic
records.summary: Sudden fear with racing heart, breathlessness or trembling.

data.trigger: Sudden fear with racing heart, breathlessness or trembling.
steps: Slow breathing: 4 seconds in, 6 seconds out
Rule out medical causes: check SpO₂, heart rate and blood sugar
data.escalate: Same day if repeated, or if medication is needed.

records.title: Crew conflict
records.summary: Ongoing tension or arguments affecting work or wellbeing.

data.trigger: Ongoing tension or arguments affecting work or wellbeing.
steps: Pause and separate tasks for a while
Use the agreed crew conflict process
Private conference with ground psychological support
data.comms_note: Small crews on long missions cannot walk away from each other.

records.title: Difficult news from home
records.summary: Bereavement or serious family news received during the mission.

data.trigger: Bereavement or serious family news received during the mission.
steps: Private call with family when the link allows
Adjust workload for the next days
Check in daily on sleep and mood
data.escalate: Next private conference, sooner if needed.
data.comms_note: Comms delay can make real-time support from home impossible.

records.title: Using an expired medicine
records.summary: The only available medicine for a condition has passed its expiry date.

data.trigger: The only available medicine for a condition has passed its expiry date.
steps: Check for a non-expired alternative in the pharmacy
Inspect for discolouration, crumbling or cloudiness
Use per flight surgeon guidance, accepting possible lower potency
data.escalate: Inform the ground at the next contact.
data.comms_note: A 2024 study found most ISS-formulary medicines would expire before a Mars mission ends.

records.title: Medicine running low
records.summary: Two or fewer doses left of a medicine.

data.trigger: Two or fewer doses left of a medicine.
steps: Check pharmacy for alternatives in the same class
Reserve remaining doses for the most serious uses
data.comms_note: Beyond low Earth orbit there is no resupply.

records.title: High cumulative radiation dose
records.summary: Cumulative dose above 50% of the career limit.

data.trigger: Cumulative dose above 50% of the career limit.
steps: Plan EVAs for quiet space weather

records.title: Suit pressure loss during EVA
records.summary: Suit pressure alarm, ear pain or breathlessness during EVA.

data.trigger: Suit pressure alarm, ear pain or breathlessness during EVA.

records.title: Dental abscess
records.summary: Throbbing toothache with swelling of the gum or face.

data.trigger: Throbbing toothache with swelling of the gum or face.
steps: Rinse with warm salt water or chlorhexidine
Temporary filling if a filling is lost
data.escalate: Same day if swelling spreads or fever develops.

steps: Check CO₂ level, hydration and sleep
Rest in a darker, quieter area
data.escalate: Immediately if sudden and severe, or with vision change, weakness or confusion.
data.comms_note: Headaches are common in flight, often linked to CO₂ and fluid shift.
